name: Learn: Helm & Kustomize
objective: CKAD › Application Deployment (20%). Goal: deploy and customize applications with Helm (scaffold a chart, install a release, override values on upgrade, inspect releases) and Kustomize (apply a base, then layer a customization) via `helm` and `kubectl apply -k` — the packaging-and-templating tasks that show up on CKAD.
description: Package and customize apps the two ways CKAD expects — Helm charts/releases/values and Kustomize bases/overlays. Scaffold a chart, install and upgrade a release overriding values, inspect it, then drive a Kustomize base and layer a customization with kubectl apply -k.

questions.title: Helm: scaffold a chart and install a release
questions.teach:
**Helm** packages Kubernetes manifests as a **chart** and tracks each deployment as a **release**. `helm create <name>` scaffolds a ready-to-run chart (a `Chart.yaml`, `values.yaml` of defaults, and `templates/` holding a Deployment, Service, ServiceAccount, HPA, and `_helpers.tpl`). `helm install <release> <chart> -n <ns>` renders the templates with those values and applies them.

**Ways to install a chart:**
- From a **local directory**: `helm install <release> ./mychart`.
- From a **packaged archive**: `helm install <release> mychart-1.0.0.tgz` (build one with `helm package ./mychart`).
- From a **repo**: `helm repo add <name> <url>` then `helm install <release> <repo>/<chart>` (optionally `--version`).
- From an **OCI registry**: `helm install <release> oci://registry/chart --version x.y.z`.

**Useful install flags:** `--create-namespace` (make the ns if missing), `--generate-name` (auto name), `-f values.yaml` / `--set key=val` (override defaults), `--dry-run` + `--debug` (render without applying — great for checking output), `--wait` (block until resources are ready).

**Exam gotchas:**
- Helm records release state in a **Secret** of type `helm.sh/release.v1` (named `sh.helm.release.v1.<release>.v<rev>`) in the release namespace — that Secret, *not* a running pod, is the source of truth for `helm list`, `upgrade`, and `rollback`. Delete it and Helm "forgets" the release.
- Releases are **namespace-scoped**: the same release name can exist in two namespaces, and `helm list`/`status` only see the `-n <ns>` you pass (`helm list -A` for all).
- `helm install` **fails** if the release name already exists — use `helm upgrade --install` to be idempotent.
- Resource names usually come from the chart (e.g. `<release>-<chart>`), so the Deployment here is `demo-webapp`, not `demo`.
- `helm create` defaults to the **nginx** image and `replicaCount: 1`.
questions.prompt:
Namespace `helm-learn` already exists. Scaffold a chart named `webapp` (anywhere on the host, e.g. under `/tmp`), then install a release named `demo` of it into `helm-learn`.

Target: a release Secret of type `helm.sh/release.v1` for release `demo` exists in `helm-learn`, AND the chart's Deployment `demo-webapp` is present there.
questions.hint: `cd /tmp && helm create webapp` scaffolds the chart. Then `helm install demo /tmp/webapp -n helm-learn`. Check with `helm list -n helm-learn` and `kubectl get deploy,secret -n helm-learn`.
questions.solution:
cd /tmp
helm create webapp
helm install demo /tmp/webapp -n helm-learn
helm list -n helm-learn
kubectl get deploy demo-webapp -n helm-learn
kubectl get secret -n helm-learn --field-selector type=helm.sh/release.v1   # sh.helm.release.v1.demo.v1

verification.description: helm release 'demo' Secret (helm.sh/release.v1) and Deployment demo-webapp exist in helm-learn

questions.title: Helm: override a value on upgrade (--set)
questions.teach:
Charts expose knobs through **values**. The scaffolded `webapp` chart defaults `replicaCount: 1`. You change a value without editing chart files using `helm upgrade <release> <chart> --set <key>=<value>` — Helm re-renders the templates with the override, patches the live objects, and creates a new **revision** of the release. Here `--set replicaCount=3` flows into the Deployment's `spec.replicas`.

**Ways to override values (lowest to highest precedence):**
- Chart's own `values.yaml` (the baseline defaults).
- One or more `-f myvalues.yaml` / `--values` files (later files override earlier).
- `--set key=value` on the CLI (overrides files; use `a.b.c=v` for nesting, `list[0]=v` for arrays, commas to set several, `\,` to escape).
- `--set-string` (force a string, e.g. a numeric tag), `--set-file key=path` (read a value from a file).

**Inspecting what values are in play:** `helm show values <chart>` (chart defaults), `helm get values <release>` (user overrides), `helm get values <release> -a` (all computed values).

**Exam gotchas:**
- `helm upgrade` **requires the chart reference again** (`helm upgrade demo /tmp/webapp ...`), not just the release name.
- `--set` values **do not persist** across upgrades unless re-passed — a later `helm upgrade` without `--set` reverts to chart defaults. `--reuse-values` keeps the previous overrides.
- Each `upgrade` bumps the **revision**; `helm history <release>` lists them and `helm rollback <release> <rev>` reverts (itself creating a new revision).
- `helm upgrade --install` creates the release if it doesn't exist, otherwise upgrades (idempotent).
- Use `--dry-run --debug` to preview the rendered manifest before applying.
questions.prompt:
Upgrade the `demo` release so its Deployment runs **3** replicas, by overriding `replicaCount` with `--set` (do not edit the chart files).

Target: Deployment `demo-webapp` in `helm-learn` has `spec.replicas: 3`.
questions.hint: `helm upgrade demo /tmp/webapp -n helm-learn --set replicaCount=3`, then `kubectl get deploy demo-webapp -n helm-learn -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}'`.
questions.solution:
helm upgrade demo /tmp/webapp -n helm-learn --set replicaCount=3
kubectl get deploy demo-webapp -n helm-learn -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}'   # 3

verification.description: demo-webapp Deployment scaled to 3 replicas via helm --set

questions.title: Helm: inspect the deployed release
questions.teach:
`helm list -n <ns>` shows every release in a namespace with its name, status, revision, chart, and app version. Under the hood Helm finds releases by their state Secrets, which carry labels `owner=helm`, `name=<release>`, and `status=deployed`. Knowing a release is `deployed` (not `failed`/`pending-upgrade`/`superseded`) confirms the last `install`/`upgrade` succeeded — the thing you'd check before `rollback` or `uninstall`.

**The inspection commands (know which shows what):**
- `helm list` (alias `helm ls`): one line per release; `-A`/`--all-namespaces` for every ns; `--filter <regex>`; `-a`/`--all` includes failed/uninstalled; `-o json|yaml` for scripting.
- `helm status <release>`: current status, last-deployed time, and the NOTES.txt.
- `helm history <release>`: every revision with its status and change-cause.
- `helm get all|manifest|values|notes|hooks <release>`: the rendered manifest / values / notes for a specific revision (`--revision N`).

**Exam gotchas:**
- `helm list` / `status` are **namespace-scoped** — forget `-n <ns>` and a release looks "missing"; use `-A` when unsure where it lives.
- Only the **newest** revision is `deployed`; previous ones become `superseded` (`-a` reveals them). A failed upgrade leaves status `failed` while the old revision still runs.
- Release state lives in the Secret `sh.helm.release.v1.<release>.v<rev>` labelled `owner=helm,name=<release>,status=deployed`; that is how `helm list` discovers releases even though no "Helm server" exists (Helm 3 is client-only).
- `helm uninstall <release>` removes the release and its state Secrets; add `--keep-history` to retain them.
questions.prompt:
Confirm the `demo` release is present and currently **deployed** in `helm-learn`.

Target: `helm list -n helm-learn` shows release `demo` with status `deployed` (its deployed release Secret carries label `name=demo`).
questions.hint: `helm list -n helm-learn` (add `--filter demo`). The deployed state Secret is labelled `name=demo,status=deployed`: `kubectl get secret -n helm-learn -l owner=helm,status=deployed,name=demo`.
questions.solution:
helm list -n helm-learn
helm status demo -n helm-learn
kubectl get secret -n helm-learn -l owner=helm,status=deployed,name=demo   # sh.helm.release.v1.demo.vN

verification.description: release 'demo' is listed as deployed in helm-learn

questions.title: Kustomize: apply a base
questions.teach:
**Kustomize** customizes plain manifests with **no templating** — a `kustomization.yaml` lists `resources` and declarative transforms, and Kustomize overlays changes onto the referenced YAML. `kubectl` has Kustomize built in: `kubectl apply -k <dir>` *builds* the directory's kustomization and applies the result. `kubectl kustomize <dir>` (or `kustomize build <dir>`) prints the rendered YAML **without applying** — use it to preview.

The base here at `/tmp/kustomize-ckad` has a `deployment.yaml` (Deployment `hello`) plus a `kustomization.yaml` that references it and pins `namespace: kustomize-learn`.

**Anatomy of a kustomization.yaml:**
- `apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1`, `kind: Kustomization` (optional but conventional).
- `resources:` — list of manifest files, directories, or remote URLs to include. (The old `bases:` field is deprecated; bases now just go in `resources`.)
- Transforms such as `namespace`, `namePrefix`/`nameSuffix`, `commonLabels`/`labels`, `commonAnnotations`, `images`, `replicas`, `patches`, `configMapGenerator`/`secretGenerator`.

**Exam gotchas:**
- The file **must** be named `kustomization.yaml` (also accepts `kustomization.yml` / `Kustomization`) and sit in the dir you point `-k` at — a wrong name gives "unable to find one of ...".
- `-k` takes a **directory** (or git URL), not a single file: `kubectl apply -k ./dir` is right, `-k file.yaml` is wrong.
- `apply -k` vs `apply -f`: `-f` applies raw manifests, `-k` builds a kustomization first. Don't mix them up.
- Preview with `kubectl kustomize <dir>` before applying to catch indentation/path errors.
- Paths in `resources:` are **relative to the kustomization.yaml**, and a base dir referenced by an overlay must itself contain a `kustomization.yaml`.
questions.prompt:
Apply the Kustomize base at `/tmp/kustomize-ckad` to the cluster.

Target: Deployment `hello` exists in namespace `kustomize-learn`.
questions.solution:
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad
kubectl get deploy hello -n kustomize-learn

verification.description: Deployment 'hello' created in kustomize-learn from the base

questions.title: Kustomize: layer a customization (namePrefix)
questions.teach:
The point of Kustomize is overlaying changes **without copying YAML**. Transforms in `kustomization.yaml` rewrite the generated output. Adding `namePrefix: prod-` makes the built Deployment's name become `prod-hello`, letting one base serve many environments (dev/staging/prod overlays referencing the same base).

**Common transforms (the CKAD toolkit):**
- `namePrefix:` / `nameSuffix:` — prepend/append to every resource name.
- `namespace:` — set the namespace on all resources.
- `commonLabels:` / `labels:` / `commonAnnotations:` — stamp labels/annotations on everything (commonLabels also updates selectors).
- `replicas:` — `- name: hello` + `count: 3` patches a Deployment's replica count by name.
- `images:` — `- name: nginx` with `newName:`/`newTag:`/`digest:` swaps the image without touching the manifest.
- `configMapGenerator:` / `secretGenerator:` — generate ConfigMaps/Secrets from literals or files (with a content hash suffix for auto-rollout).
- `patches:` — strategic-merge or JSON6902 patches targeted by kind/name for arbitrary field changes.

**Overlay pattern:** an overlay dir has its own `kustomization.yaml` whose `resources:` points at the base dir (e.g. `../../base`) and then adds the transforms above.

**Exam gotchas:**
- `namePrefix`/`nameSuffix` rewrite names **and update references** (e.g. a Service's selector-driven references, volume/configMap refs) so things still wire up — but downstream consumers must use the new name (`prod-hello`).
- `configMapGenerator`/`secretGenerator` append a **hash suffix** to the name so a data change forces a rollout; disable per-generator with `options: { disableNameSuffixHash: true }`.
- `commonLabels` injects into selectors too — changing it on an existing Deployment can be rejected because `spec.selector` is immutable; prefer `labels` (without `includeSelectors`) when you only want metadata labels.
- Always `kubectl kustomize <dir>` first to confirm the rendered names/namespace before `apply -k`.
- Re-applying after adding `namePrefix` creates a **new** `prod-hello` Deployment; the old `hello` is not renamed in place (it would be orphaned unless pruned).
questions.prompt:
Edit `/tmp/kustomize-ckad/kustomization.yaml` to add `namePrefix: prod-`, then re-apply with `kubectl apply -k`.

Target: a Deployment named `prod-hello` exists in namespace `kustomize-learn`.
questions.hint: Add a top-level line `namePrefix: prod-` to `/tmp/kustomize-ckad/kustomization.yaml`, then `kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad`. Verify with `kubectl get deploy prod-hello -n kustomize-learn`.
questions.solution:
printf '\nnamePrefix: prod-\n' >> /tmp/kustomize-ckad/kustomization.yaml
kubectl apply -k /tmp/kustomize-ckad
kubectl get deploy prod-hello -n kustomize-learn

verification.description: namePrefix overlay produced Deployment 'prod-hello' in kustomize-learn
